correctness.rationale: The last creation vertex gives an exact dichotomy. If isolated, it is always accepted and appends to the greedy output without changing earlier decisions. If dominating, it is universal: with probability \(1/k\) it is first and yields the singleton output, while otherwise the first earlier accepted vertex blocks it and the restricted earlier order is uniform, yielding \(P_k(x)=x/k+(k-1)P_{k-1}(x)/k\). Iterating this recursion gives the stated product probabilities, and the support sets are exactly the recursively propagated maximal independent sets. Since every dominating-created vertex has vertex \(1\) as a neighbor, no output with a dominating vertex exceeds the all-zero independent set; the maximum-success product follows by telescoping before the second zero and multiplying preservation factors afterward. Exact brute force over all 127 creation sequences through order seven matched every output probability and corollary across 347741 permutation checks.

value.rationale: The claim converts a canonical structural representation of threshold graphs into the full finite law of a widely studied randomized greedy algorithm, not merely one expectation or an enumeration. It exposes the exact sampling bias among maximal independent sets, yields expectation and variance in one pass, and gives a closed probability that greedy is actually maximum. These are reusable benchmark formulas for randomized MIS analysis and for validating samplers on a graph class where every maximal independent set is already structurally understood.
